title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
This incident shows a deployment failure in a cryptocurrency trading platform's security controls. Scammers gained access to a legitimate app and inserted a fake AI-generated website between the user and his real account information, so he saw fabricated balances and transaction history that matched his deposits. The system lacked verification steps to confirm the user was seeing authentic account data, such as server-side validation displayed to the user or alerts when account access occurred from unusual locations or devices.

The failure happened at the point where the user viewed his account. A human review of the account activity, withdrawal patterns, or the unusual spike in deposits could have flagged the case before the largest withdrawals were attempted. The platform did not appear to have real-time fraud detection or spending limits that would have caught the pattern of increasingly large deposits followed by a withdrawal request.

It is not established whether the platform knew its security had been compromised, whether the scammers had legitimate access credentials, or what technical methods they used to insert the fake website into the user's view of the app.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a sophisticated cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. The scammer convinced Jerry Dunaway to invest through a legitimate-looking mobile trading app, building trust by allowing him to make small trades and withdraw funds initially. However, the scammers had created an AI-generated fake website that displayed false information about his account balance and investments, tricking him into depositing increasingly larger amounts of money.

When Jerry attempted to withdraw a larger sum last week, he discovered the funds were gone and contacted police. Gwinnett County investigators determined the app was real but the scammers manipulated his view of the account through the ghost site. The couple is now warning others about the sophisticated tactics used by these criminals. Police say victims in these cases rarely recover their money. To help support themselves, their children have started a GoFundMe campaign while the family works with authorities on the case.
